kitDescription: Helm (Treasure) is a Water-element sniper Attacker on Burst III who charges every shot. Each full-charge shot does three things at once: it heals the whole team a little, dumps 14.31% into the team's burst gauge (a large rotation accelerator on a ~1.4-second shot cycle), and tacks an extra hit worth 178.98% of her ATK onto whatever she shot. When the last round of her six-shot magazine lands, the whole team gets +14.64% critical rate on NORMAL ATTACKS ONLY for 5 seconds — it does not lift crit on anyone's skill procs or burst damage. On entering Full Burst she gives every ally +27.87% Attack Damage for 10 seconds, and she passively adds a small amount of interruption-part damage that does nothing at all against a boss with no parts. Her burst fires one huge 8236.8%-of-ATK shot at the strongest enemy, gives the team 10 seconds of attack-driven healing, and raises her own charge-damage multiplier by 158.4% for her next 10 shots — which, on a 6-round magazine, necessarily carries across a reload.

burst.formulaCheck: No HP pool and no lifesteal StatKey ⇒ the magnitude 54.45% is unmodelable under any encoding. The only board channel is downstream recovery consumers. Neither treatment can be checked against the damage formula; the discriminator is which residue is closer to 'recovery keeps taking effect for 10 sec'.
burst.explanation: JUDGE RULING (the question S6 escalated): the driver's event-window is ACCEPTABLE and marginally more faithful than unmodeled-verbatim. In game the recovery genuinely takes effect repeatedly across the window, so zero recovery events is also a wrong residue; the driver fabricates no magnitude, and a fixed 1/s cadence does not machine-gun the consumer (S6's stated objection does not apply to what was actually shipped). It is a DOCUMENTED_GAP, not FAITHFUL, because the 1s tick cadence has no measured basis — it is an engine-available stand-in, named as such in caveats. Residual risk to watch: it is a SECOND recovery source emitting ~10 firings × 4 allies per burst; any future consumer that COUNTS recoveries (rather than being refreshed by them) would be over-fed. Board-inert today because S1's ~1.5s heal already saturates crown-style consumers, and H8 pins the window under a fixture that strips both S1's heal and crown's own — a correct isolation per Method C. NB the blind's own test accepts either treatment (documented || encoded), so S6's preference was never enforced by its own harness.

gotchas.summary: The override note asserts a 90-frame SR shot cycle (60f charge + 30f recovery) and calls it 'the validated 90-frame cycle', but both mechanics SSOT docs put helm's MEASURED cycle at 82 frames (60f charge + 22f bolt/release latency = 1.37s) — and cite HELM's own recording as the source. If the engine ships 30f, her three per-pull kit lines all under-fire by ~7% over 180s; if it ships 22f, the note misdocuments the constant.
gotchas.evidence: game-mechanics.md §4: 'SR bolt cycle: +22 frames after each shot (MEASURED: helm recording, 1.37s cycle = 60f charge + 22f)'; damage-calculation.md §2a repeats '22-frame release latency (MEASURED)'. Driver note: 'CHARFIX: universal SR bolt-recovery rule (60f charge + 30f recovery) reproduces the validated 90-frame cycle (no charFixes needed)'. 90f = 1.5s ≠ the measured 1.37s. Magazine arithmetic: 6×90+141 = 681f ⇒ ~95 pulls/180s vs 6×82+141 = 633f ⇒ ~102 pulls/180s (~7.4% fewer riders, heals and 14.31% gauge fills). NOT caught by S5 or S6 — all three agents worked from kit prose and never touched the weapon-side constant, so this is an uncorroborated single-reader find.
gotchas.suggestedFix: VERIFY, do not adjust to fit: (1) read the SR bolt/release-recovery constant in src/engine/sim.ts (near the charge block / charFixes.noBoltRecovery) and compare against 22f; (2) count helm 'shot' events in a 180s control run — ~102 ⇒ 82f, ~95 ⇒ 90f. If the engine ships 30f, the faithful value is the MEASURED 22f from the helm recording and the fix is engine-wide across all SR units (REPORT ONLY — out of scope for a per-unit kit verdict, do not land it inside this gauntlet slot). If the engine already ships 22f, correct the override note's '60f + 30f = validated 90-frame cycle' sentence, which currently contradicts the SSOT.

verdictRationale: All 9 kit lines are represented and 8 are FAITHFUL against prose + formula SSOT; the 9th (burst lifesteal) is a DOCUMENTED_GAP, so faithfulness is 9/9 = 1.0 with zero silent drops (unmodeled{} is empty and every line is traceable to a block or, for the gauge fill, to the SSOT-named data/gauge-per-shot.json mechanism). Convergence is RED out of the box (6/30 blind assertions fail) but ALL SIX are RECON_ERRORs on encoding details the blinds could only guess at: the StatKey ('chargeDamagePct' vs the schema-and-SSOT-correct chargeDamageMultPct — damage-calculation §1d names Helm's burst as the multiplier class), and the gauge-fill LOCATION (an override fillGauge block vs the data file that game-mechanics §6 explicitly designates for helm). Every kit-line assertion the blind derived correctly passed against the shipped override unchanged — including three discriminations the driver's own file does not carry: fullBurstEnter-vs-burstCast by event order, the rider's rangeApplied===false and both-FB-states coverage, and the nuke's fbMajorApplied===false. That closes S2b's two advisory residuals. On the one question escalated to me: the driver's 10-tick/1s recovery window is the better of the two available treatments for the 54.45% lifesteal — it fabricates no magnitude, it is not the per-hit stream S6 warned about, and unmodeled-verbatim would emit ZERO recovery events across a window in which recovery demonstrably does take effect; I keep it as DOCUMENTED_GAP rather than FAITHFUL because the 1s cadence is invented, and the standing risk is that it is a second recovery SOURCE (≈10 firings × 4 allies per burst) that any future recovery-COUNTING consumer would over-feed. One real gotcha, unranked by anyone before me: the override note's SR cadence claim (60f + 30f = 'validated 90-frame cycle') contradicts both SSOT docs, which put helm's MEASURED cycle at 60f + 22f = 1.37s and cite her own recording — a ~7% swing in the firing rate that carries all three of her per-pull lines. It does not gate GO (it is an engine-wide weapon constant, not a kit encoding, and I could not execute anything this turn to confirm which value the engine ships), but it is the top item for the owner. Same-model residual to spot-check, ranked: (1) that SR cadence constant — every agent in this gauntlet read prose only, so nothing here is independent evidence about the weapon side; (2) the carried ⚑ that 'hitting a target with Full Charge' == shotFired for both the S1 heal/gauge tier and the 178.98% rider, which needs a helm focus video showing one rider popup per charged shot; (3) a documentation slip worth fixing while nearby — the note's rl3 corroboration reads '59.73 = 8.4 + 3x14.31', which sums to 51.33; the identity actually closes exactly as 3 × (5.6 + 14.31) = 16.8 + 42.93 = 59.73 using the boss-doubled 5.6%/shot, so the 14.31 datamined value is MORE strongly corroborated than the note's own arithmetic suggests. Method caveat, stated plainly: I had no tools this turn, so the S5-vs-driver run counts are the driver's reported execution; I independently verified each of the six reds by reading the blind predicate against the shipped override and confirmed each is a predicate mismatch, not a behavioural divergence.
